cards.title: Unit 1: Challenges
body: This unit is called Challenges. The grammar is finite and non-finite clauses.
The notes below give the rule, the form, examples and the mistakes that lose marks.
Examples use Eritrean places. The practice questions are original.

cards.title: Finite and non-finite clauses
rule: A finite verb has a tense and a subject. It can be the main verb of a sentence.
Non-finite forms do not show tense by themselves: the to-infinitive, the -ing form, and the past participle.
A sentence needs at least one finite verb. Non-finite clauses can add information: Opening the door, he walked in.
cards.pattern: finite = tense + subject; non-finite = to-verb / -ing / past participle

examples.note: The -ing phrase is not a full sentence.
Want is finite; to rest is not.

cards.title: Forms to learn
head: Form
Finite?
Example
rows: She wants to open the door.

cards.title: Common mistakes
body: To go home is not a sentence.
Every full sentence needs a finite verb.

cards.title: Worked example
cards.problem: A learner wrote: Opening the door. Fix it and say why.

steps.text: The correct pattern is: finite = tense + subject; non-finite = to-verb / -ing / past participle.
The -ing phrase is not a full sentence.
A correct sentence is: Opening the door, she smiled.
Compare with a good model: She opened the window.

cards.meaning: A verb with tense and a subject.
An infinitive, -ing form or participle without its own tense.

cards.title: A short text: Challenges
paras: In Asmara, students meet after class to revise finite and non-finite clauses together.
They write one correct sentence each, then they correct a partner's mistake.
They say the group helps them remember more than reading alone.

questions.q: What do the students do after class?
questions.a: They revise finite and non-finite clauses together.

questions.q: What do they say helps them remember?

glossary.meaning: A verb with tense and a subject.
An infinitive, -ing form or participle without its own tense.
The clause that can stand as the sentence.
A group of words without a finite verb.

tips.text: Ask: can this group of words stand alone as a sentence? If not, it is probably non-finite.

pairs.b: A verb with tense and a subject.

questions.q: Which group contains a finite verb?
why: A finite verb shows tense and agrees with a subject. Opened is finite. To open and opening are non-finite.
questions.tip: Read every option. Cross out the ones that break the grammar rule, then choose.
questions.label: 1. Which group contains a finite verb?

questions.q: ___ the door, he walked in. The -ing phrase is non-finite.
why: Opening has no tense of its own. It is a non-finite clause. The finite verb is walked.
questions.label: 2. Opening the door

questions.q: A finite clause can stand alone as a sentence. A non-finite clause usually cannot.
why: She laughed is a complete finite clause. Laughing loudly is not a full sentence.
questions.label: 3. Finite clause

questions.q: In 'I want to rest', to rest is the finite verb.
why: Want is finite. To rest is a non-finite infinitive.
questions.label: 4. to rest

questions.q: The man ___ by the gate is my uncle. (stand / standing / stood)
why: A non-finite -ing clause can modify a noun: the man standing by the gate.
questions.label: 5. standing

questions.q: In one sentence, define a finite verb.
questions.answer: A finite verb has a tense and a subject. It can be the main verb of a sentence.
why: Non-finite forms do not show tense by themselves.
questions.label: 6. define finite verb

why: Tired after the walk has no finite verb.
questions.label: 7. non-finite clause

questions.q: Students in Asmara revise together. What helps them remember?
why: The text says the group helps them remember more.
questions.label: 8. reading

questions.q: Give the main idea of the Asmara revision text in a few words.
questions.answer: Students in Asmara revise together because it helps them remember.
why: The main idea is the point of the whole text.
questions.label: 9. main idea

questions.q: Which word begins a subordinate clause?

questions.answer: Words that commonly go together, such as make a mistake.

questions.q: Which is the best topic sentence about saving water in Asmara?

options.B: Families in Asmara can save water in three simple ways.

why: A topic sentence names the subject and the controlling idea.
The frequency adverb goes before an ordinary verb.
